name: Damaris
title: Believing woman from Athens
summary: Damaris was a woman from Athens who came to faith in Jesus Christ after hearing the apostle Paul speak at the Areopagus. She is one of very few individuals mentioned by name among those converted in Athens, suggesting she held a somewhat prominent position in society. Her conversion shows that the gospel reached both men and women in the Greek world.

keyEvents.title: Paul speaks at the Areopagus
keyEvents.description: The apostle Paul was brought to the Areopagus in Athens to explain his teaching about Jesus and the resurrection to the philosophically minded Athenians.

keyEvents.title: Paul preaches the resurrection
keyEvents.description: Paul proclaimed the true God and the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, which sparked mixed reactions among the listeners at the Areopagus.

keyEvents.title: Damaris comes to faith
keyEvents.description: After Paul's speech at the Areopagus, Damaris joined him and came to believe. She is mentioned by name along with Dionysius the Areopagite as one of the few who became believers in Athens.

keyEvents.title: Paul arrives in Athens
keyEvents.description: Paul arrived in Athens and was distressed by all the idols in the city. He began to reason with Jews and God-fearing people in the synagogue and with people in the marketplace.

keyEvents.title: The Spread of the Gospel Among the Greeks
keyEvents.description: Damaris' conversion is a testimony that the gospel took root even in Athens, the intellectual and philosophical center, and reached both women and men in the Greek world.
